headline: Billionaire Peter Thiel told Nashville lecture audiences that Barack Obama and Pope Leo XIV oppose AI mainly to win popularity, according to recordings Politico obtained.
score_reason: Notable remarks by a major AI investor, but a relayed account of lectures with a satirical edge; no policy action.
importance_line: It shows how a leading AI investor frames regulation as a moral and political fight with the pope, with Thiel's side coming from recordings and no comment from his representatives; Gizmodo notes his wealth is heavily invested in AI.
summary: Politico reports, as relayed by Gizmodo, that billionaire Peter Thiel told Nashville audiences that government attempts to regulate AI are evil and that Barack Obama and Pope Leo XIV oppose AI because it is unpopular and they want to boost their own standing. Thiel's complaint appears to be the pope's earlier first encyclical (a formal papal letter), which Gizmodo says tied the AI era to "new forms of dehumanization"; the article gives no date for that letter and we did not carry it.
notes: Read at Gizmodo; the original is Politico's Decoded newsletter, link not given in the article. Reply story: Thiel answers Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical.
